subject: Proposed 4-week assessment sprint & success gates — Petrum AI
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Donovan <claire@petrumai.com>, Samir Patel <samir@petrumai.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Mar 2028 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed 4-week assessment sprint & success gates — Petrum AI

Hi Claire & Samir,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — really appreciated the candid product context and the examples you shared around extracting structured metadata from support tickets. As promised, I put together a concise proposal for a 4-week assessment sprint (POC-lite) that we believe will demonstrate Redwood Inference’s ability to meet your latency and cost targets while preserving end-to-end data controls.

High-level proposal (4 weeks):
- Week 0 (Prep, 2–3 days): access, dataset handoff, and security checklist (Karthik will run tech onboarding).
- Week 1 (Baseline & ingestion): run sample batch over historical tickets, measure token distribution, baseline latency/cost.
- Week 2 (Optimizations): enable prefix caching + quantized runtime; tune batching policy and observe quality drift on evaluation prompts.
- Week 3 (Integration & validation): small integration (staging), run acceptance tests on 200 live tickets.
- Deliverables: performance report (latency P50/P95), cost per 1k tokens, evaluation against success criteria, and a short runbook for production rollout.

Proposed success criteria (pass/fail checkpoints):
1) Average inference latency (P50) <= 350ms for 512-token requests in staging.
2) P95 latency <= 1.2s under expected batching profile.
3) Model output accuracy: intent classification F1 >= 0.85 on the canonical 250-sample eval set.
4) End-to-end cost projection within 25% of the target cost you shared.
5) No data leaves your VPC or S3 (we’ll run with private deployment settings).

Ownership & roles:
- Petrum AI: provide sample dataset (+ schema), credentials for a staging S3, and a primary technical lead for integration (Claire).
- Redwood: tech onboarding (Karthik), inference config and tuning (Marcus), engagement lead & success metrics (me).

Next steps I propose:
1) Confirm acceptance of the 4-week scope and the success criteria above.
2) Share staging S3 access and the sample eval set by EOD Friday (Mar 16).
3) Kickoff call to align on timelines — can we do Mon Mar 19 9:00am PT?

I attached a brief POC checklist and a technical questionnaire to speed the kickoff. If any of the success gates look off, call them out and we’ll adjust.

Best,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Manager | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Subject: Re: Proposed 4-week assessment sprint & success gates — Petrum AI

Thanks Soojin — this looks very actionable and well scoped. A couple of quick notes from our side before we lock dates: 

- The 512-token target is fine, though a subset of our tickets average closer to 200 tokens; can you validate metrics across both 200/512 slices?
- For the accuracy gate, can we use our internal labeling set (we'll provide the 250-sample eval) but also reserve a 100-sample holdout for acceptance?
- We need the tech questionnaire answered for our security review (SOC/SAML questions highlighted).

We can get you staging S3 access and the eval set by end-of-day Friday 16th. Monday the 19th at 9:00am PT works for Claire and Samir.

One ask: during Week 2 optimizations, we’d like a short run showing how quantization affects output fidelity (notes on recommended quantization profile and a small AB sample). Is that possible?

—Claire
Claire Donovan
Head of Data Products | Petrum AI
claire@petrumai.com | +1 (212) 555-9842

Quick internal note (tech onboarding / capacity):

Notes and config we should prep before the kickoff:
- Staging cluster: 2 x A10G (or equivalent) with 16GB batch-capacity target. That should hit the latency targets for 200–512 tokens with continuous batching.
- Model variants: suggest starting with the open-llama-13B quant-friendly variant; keep a float16 variant on standby for quality checks.
- KV cache behavior: set per-session TTL = 5m for the POC to simulate active sessions without large memory growth.
- Logging & audit: enable request-level latency and token-count logs to S3 (separate bucket), redact PHI fields per their schema.

Prep tasks for Marcus / Monica: draft the acceptance test scripts (200/512 token slices) and the AB fidelity test for quantization. I’ll prepare the onboarding checklist and a short network diagram to include in the security answers.

Karthik
Senior Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>

Claire — perfect, thanks for the clarifications. To address your asks:
- We will report latency metrics across both 200- and 512-token slices in the baseline report.
- We'll use your 250-sample labeled set for evaluation and hold out the 100-sample acceptance set as requested.
- Marcus will run the AB quantization fidelity checks and include a short analysis documenting any regressions and recommended profile.

I attached an updated POC checklist and the short security answers draft (Petrum_Technical_Questions.pdf) — Karthik, please confirm the network diagram stub before we send the doc to their security team.

Confirming kickoff: Mon Mar 19 9:00am PT — sending a calendar invite now (you should receive a separate invite).

Immediate asks for Petrum prior to kickoff:
1) Staging S3 credentials with a read-only service account for Redwood.
2) The 250-sample eval set + schema.
3) Point of contact for any firewall/VPN egress configuration (we'll provide IPs).

If Petrum is comfortable we can run Week 0 activities the morning after kickoff so the team has one full week for baseline work.

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.

Best,
Soojin
